items.q: What does Robert Greene mean by power if not CEOs and tyrants?
items.a: Power is an **intrinsic human need** — the feeling you can **influence your environment**. Misery hits when you can't move spouse, kids, or colleagues; he cites Malcolm X that **absolute powerlessness corrupts even more** than absolute power.

items.q: Is public role-playing fake, or is it human?
items.a: Social masks are normal primate play (18th-century café style). The neurosis starts when you **confuse the role with your essence** — **self-control** and tailored appearance come before controlling others.

items.q: Why call seduction a high form of power?
items.a: You make people feel **pleasure and interest** so **resistance lowers** without them realizing. Great seducers are **outer-directed** — absorb the other's psychology and reflect it back, instead of preaching an internal monologue.

items.q: What behaviors kill attraction on dates?
items.a: **Anti-seducers** moralize, preach politics, radiate **insecurity**, or go cheap on spirit (discount-code first dates). **Vulnerability draws**; insecurity repels. Low effort (jeans + pub) signals "you're not worth it."

items.q: Can you fake confidence until it works?
items.a: No — bravado reads as insecurity via **micro-expressions**. **Real confidence comes from accomplishments** and skills; at 21 you may have little substrate yet. Fix the **inner security** and gestures radiate; don't police every tic.

Body language is **pre-linguistic (~95% of communication)** — words lie, **voice and posture don't**. Learn fake vs real smile, feet angle, pecking forward vs leaning back (Erickson mastered this while paralyzed).

items.q: Should you chase "passion" as life's task?
items.a: Greene finds "passion" cringe. **Life's task** is the deep childhood connection that **survives tedium** (piano scales for a year). He wrote *Mastery* because young men mistook Power/Seduction for the whole game.

items.q: What job should you take in your early twenties?
items.a: Prefer **apprenticeship over paycheck** — take the role that pays **~1/3** if you **learn the most**. Be a sponge, not an impresser; learning by doing matches how the brain wires.

items.q: Why does Greene say connection feels harder now?
items.a: Drivers of the **dating recession / male loneliness** stack: apps, porn, **instant-gratification culture**, and lost in-person **body-language fluency**. Apps can't replace skin — **mirror neurons** need real rejection reps.

items.q: What did his 2018 stroke change about power and gratitude?
items.a: Left-side paralysis made **powerlessness visceral** (**death-ground urgency**). Recovery leaned on **12+ years of unbroken meditation**, writing, wife's support, and reframing self-pity — don't take walking, typing, or swimming for granted.
